extracted.intended_audience: comedy fans and UK entertainment industry observers
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing boundaries, audience reaction, and consequences of offensive comedy in the context of a high-profile UK comedian's gag. Focuses on what is considered unacceptable (especially regarding vulnerable people), broadcaster responsibilities, audience relations, and legal/public fallout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Children (especially disabled) should be off-limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Quote: 'Children, especially a disabled youngster, should be off-limits.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Context: Andre's representative argues that targeting children — and in particular disabled children — is unacceptable. Example in article: Frankie Boyle's joke about Harvey, a disabled eight-year-old, sparked anger. Use this as a clear boundary when judging or producing material: avoid jokes that target minors or exploit disabilities. Antipattern: using a child's disability as the punchline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not imply sexual violence by/on a child
rubrics_metrics.description: Katie Price: 'to suggest, let alone think funny, that Harvey may sexually attack me is vile and deeply unfair.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Context: Jokes suggesting sexual harm involving children cross major ethical and reputational lines. Guidance: treat sexual-violence implications involving minors as off-limits; expect severe public backlash. Antipattern: framing a joke that posits sexual acts involving a child, even as hyperbole or shock.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadcasters should make content expectations clear
rubrics_metrics.description: Channel 4: 'People know what to expect with Frankie. We make it very clear about what type of content his show contains.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance for producers/networks: provide clear warnings/positioning about a show's tone and likely offensiveness so audiences can make informed choices. For evaluation: consider whether adequate viewers' expectations/warnings were given. Example: channel defending airing because audience knows Boyle's style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offensiveness and public disgust as evaluation metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Public reaction in the article: 'absolutely disgusted and sickened' and descriptions of the joke as 'offensive sick joke.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use measures of public outrage, strong emotional language in statements, and moral condemnation as signals that material has crossed perceived social norms. Guidance: weigh intensity of public language when assessing a joke's acceptability and reputational harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential for legal action when jokes target individuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Katie Price 'has asked her lawyers to see if any further action can be taken.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: recognize that targeted jokes about named individuals (or identifiable people) can trigger legal scrutiny (defamation, harassment, other claims). Producers and performers should consider legal exposure and counsel when material singles out private individuals, especially vulnerable ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience relations: offer refunds/alternatives when events disrupted
rubrics_metrics.description: Boyle angered fans by 'refusing to offer refunds or organise an alternative show for the 4,500 people who couldn’t get to his last gig in Glasgow because of poor weather.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance for performers/promoters: keep good customer relations by offering refunds or alternatives for cancelled/disrupted shows. Antipattern: refusing refunds leads to anger and harms reputation; cite as a separate source of controversy beyond content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience metrics (attendance/viewership) reflect acceptability
rubrics_metrics.description: Article: 'audiences for Tramdol Nights have slipped by a third.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use attendance and viewership decline as quantitative feedback about audience tolerance and the commercial consequences of controversial content. Guidance: monitor ratings/attendance to assess whether material is harming a programme's viability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performer reputation and decency as informal criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Katie Price's statement: 'If Mr Boyle had a tenth of his courage and decency, he would know...' (criticizing Boyle's moral judgment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating comedic material, consider broader judgments about a performer's decency and whether their material aligns with social expectations of courage/responsibility. This is a subjective reputational metric rather than a strict rule, but it influences public response and industry support.
